raw_response:
I am 75. I never went to school, not one day. My father put the hoe in my hand when I was small, and I have farmed this ground for 50 years. I know every corner of my 14 mu. Ten mu I plant with wheat after the autumn, and when the wheat comes off in June I put maize straight into the same ground. The other 4 mu I plant cotton so my wife and daughter-in-law can pick it, and we sell it to the buyer who drives his truck to the village.

I don't read books. I watch what works. For wheat, I spread one full bag of compound fertilizer and half a bag of urea on each mu before sowing. When the wheat turns green after winter, I spread another half bag of urea. I run the rotary tiller before planting. I water three times from my well: once after sowing if the autumn is dry, once when the wheat shoots up in spring, and once when the heads fill. I spray twice, for weeds and bugs. Last year I got about 500 kg per mu, and I expect the same if the frost doesn't cheat me.

For maize, I buy hybrid seeds from the shop, the yellow kind with fat ears. I put one bag of compound in the row when planting, and when the plants are knee-high I spread more urea, about one and a half bags per mu. There is no time to plow between wheat harvest and maize sowing, so the machine drills it straight into the wheat stubble. I water twice: when the stalks grow fast, and when the ears swell. I spray twice. I expect 600 kg per mu.

For cotton, I plough deep first because cotton roots need soft soil. I plant the same seeds I have used for years, the kind that fights bollworms. Each mu gets one bag of compound and half a bag of urea. I water three times: when the seedlings are small, when the white flowers open, and when the bolls get fat. I spray three times. My women pick it by hand. I expect 250 kg of seed cotton per mu.

I watch my neighbors. Old Li used less fertilizer last year to save money, and his wheat turned yellow and short. I will not make that mistake. Every bag of fertilizer costs real money, but losing yield is a disaster. My son works in the city and sends money home, so I buy what I need. If last year was good, I change nothing.
